KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) has called for an urgent meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border.
Its representative Dr R. Manivannan said the meeting would allow Anwar to hear directly from families of those still uncontactable.
He also urged the government to mobilise all available diplomatic, search and rescue, forensic and intelligence resources to locate and identify the missing and bring them home with dignity.
"Now entering the ninth day, we believe the prime minister's direct intervention could help expedite coordination, strengthen diplomatic efforts and ensure every available resource is mobilised to locate the missing Malaysians.
"We seek the prime minister's support and leadership, as well as a clear action plan to bring our loved ones home. This is not a political appeal, but a humanitarian plea from families seeking answers and hoping for their safe return," he said at a press conference here today.
Manivannan also welcomed Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim's concern over the affected Malaysians and his call for Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures.
He said the King had also called for the latest information on Malaysians' safety and whereabouts to be conveyed to their families.
"For the families, His Majesty's concern is deeply appreciated, and we hope it will translate into immediate, coordinated and tangible action on the ground.
"Families should not have to repeatedly seek information on the whereabouts and status of their loved ones," he said.
Manivannan also reiterated the families' call for confirmation letters saying that those remained missing to be issued immediately, as previously indicated by the authorities.
"This should not remain an unresolved administrative matter while families are facing an unprecedented humanitarian crisis," he said.
As of yesterday, 36 Malaysians remained uncontactable in China and 55 in Nepal following severe flash floods and landslides in Nepal's Rasuwa district on Aug 26.
The disaster's death toll has risen to 1,220, while 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, remain missing.
